data.text: Check this tool - https://www.accrete.ai/why-accrete and research it and see if there are ideas we can pick up for ddflow to implement, as well as separately, would ddflow be easy to integrate with accrete and give me opinion, phase + tasks for the gaps, with proper dependencies and wave to implement

data.note: Operator-requested research already done by this session; the doc task is unrelated to the docs-wave hold it inherits (hold is only a scheduling order). Forcing past the inherited phase hold, nothing else.

data.budget: about 20 fetches, no purchase or contact
data.claim: Accrete is a closed, sales-led vendor of a 'Knowledge Engine Platform' (context graph plus expert agents) for enterprises and of Argus for US government; it sells outcomes and pilots, not a developer product.
data.falsifier: A public developer portal or self-serve signup for the Knowledge Engine.
data.mechanism: Pages describe a context graph (typed entities, relationships, provenance, temporal ordering), orchestrated expert agents, memory consolidation, grounded citations, per-customer permissioning; 'book a demo' is the only call to action; deployment is a 3-step pilot (ground 2-4 weeks, one workflow, scale).
data.probe_output: why-accrete: 'context layer ... records the reasoning behind decisions'; page lists no API, MCP or SDK. enterprise: pilot 2-4 weeks, 'Book a demo', no pricing. government: Argus, FedRAMP High 'design standard' (not stated as authorised), classified use 4 contract years. trust.accrete.ai: SOC 2 Type 1/2, CMMC, DoD IL4/IL5, HIPAA, ITAR listed. blog: 'Agents as a Service - microservice for agent orchestration', 'Okta, RBAC', 'forward-deployed engineering model with MCP servers' (no detail).
data.question: What is Accrete (accrete.ai) and who is it for?

data.claim: No public API, SDK, OpenAPI, MCP endpoint or webhook documentation was found; the only mention is 'forward-deployed engineering model with MCP servers' in one blog post, with no endpoint, schema or setup.
data.falsifier: A docs site, OpenAPI file or MCP server URL published by Accrete.
data.mechanism: Delivery is licensed products, pilots and partner marketplaces (Snowflake, Databricks, Carahsoft); integration is done by Accrete engineers per customer, so no self-serve contract exists to specify an adapter against.
data.probe: WebSearch 'Accrete AI Knowledge Engine context graph API MCP docs' (extended); WebFetch github.com/api-evangelist/accrete-ai apis.yml; WebFetch accrete.ai/llms.txt and /platform
data.probe_output: search: 'no public developer API, SDK or MCP documentation'. catalog (third party, REPORTED): apis field empty; docs.accrete.ai 404, api.accrete.ai 530; auth/pricing 'Unknown'. accrete.ai/llms.txt 404; accrete.ai/platform 404 (ke-platform is the live path). Absence is limited to what was reachable unauthenticated.
data.question: Does Accrete publish an API, SDK, MCP server or webhook documentation ddflow could build against?

data.claim: The numbers are vendor-reported marketing with no stated dataset, method or independent verification; the page itself labels its growth chart illustrative.
data.falsifier: A linked methodology or third-party reproduction.
data.mechanism: The pages cite 'August 2026 publications' and customer anecdotes (entertainment company, investment fund, insurer) with no linked paper; the architecture post gives no evals, no schema and no method for causal strength.
data.question: Are Accrete's performance claims (58% lower token cost, 2x tasks, 19 of 34 tacit facts vs 1 for RAG, 92% accuracy) evidenced?

data.claim: ddflow has no MCP client and no outbound query path; it has user-definable companions (registers servers into agent configs), an egress-door mechanism for sensitivity, reviewer-trust and approval primitives, a read-only sibling-log observer, export kinds and an MCP server; client and remote pieces are queued (RQM-mcp-client, RQM-sources, KB-*, PM-descriptor, CP-notify-sinks, P-remote.serve).
data.falsifier: A shipped MCP client or HTTP service client module in ddflow/.
data.mechanism: companions.load overlays project companions.toml on the shipped list; services/egress.py withholds labelled records at named doors; services/external.py only reads a sibling event log; RQM-mcp-client is open (research doc requirements-management.md gap 7).
data.probe: read ddflow/services/companions.py (load, register), egress.py, external.py, reviewer_trust.py; docs/ddflow/research/requirements-management.md row 7; ddflow show RQM-mcp-client SX-egress-door KB-envelope
data.probe_output: companions.load: 'The shipped registry, overlaid by the project's own'; egress.Egress.withholds(door, fields); external.py: 'reads the sibling's event log -- read-only'; RQM-mcp-client state open; SX-egress-door state open.
data.question: What integration seams does ddflow have today for talking to an external knowledge service?

data.claim: Nearly all: rationale and ruled-out log (D-reasoning-log, B-am-capture, B-dec-model), provenance/validity (KB-envelope, KB-attest, B-security-provenance), permissioning (KB-scope, KB-auth, SE-sensitivity), outcome feedback and pruning (P-lessons.recurrence/.effect/.curate, PL-staleness, P-observe.effect), citations (RQM-reviewer, RQM-ack); D-graph-scope-r1 declines a knowledge-graph memory.
data.falsifier: A listed Accrete feature with no counterpart id.
data.mechanism: The queue already holds P-lessons, P-decisions, P-agent-memory, P-knowledge-hub, P-requirements, P-observe; only four narrow gaps remain.
data.probe_output: P-lessons 12 tasks, P-agent-memory 15, P-observe 14, P-knowledge-hub 24, P-decisions 17, P-requirements 27; recall surfaced D-graph-scope-r1 and D-reasoning-log; the duplicate check on this note listed all of the counterpart ids above.
data.question: Which of Accrete's ideas does ddflow already do or plan?

data.reason: same ideas (provenance, validity, scope); export edges align with KB-envelope
outcome feedback, staleness, curation already planned there
RQM-mcp-client and RQM-sources are the inbound half; consult-out is the outbound half
ddflow as MCP server for another agent platform: profiles, scoped tokens
repeat rate of recorded lessons; the probe measures what should have been recorded
curate merges lessons; this distils memories

chunk_findings.detail: The change is the output of an agent run (`ACF-research`, phase `P-accrete-fit`) but contains no self-assessment of ddflow itself and no filed-defects/duplicate check, as required by [D-ddflow-self-assessment-r2]. The doc identifies ddflow gaps such as `RQM-mcp-client open`, `ACF-consult-out`, `ACF-why-export`, and `SX-egress-door open` only as future tasks, not as filed defects, and it does not record whether any observed ddflow bug, misbehavior, or missing feature is new, duplicated, or already corrected. The single-file manifest shows no separate self-assessment artifact in this change.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md:1

chunk_findings.detail: [D-ddflow-self-assessment-r2] The newly added self-assessment still does not account for the ddflow missing features this very document discovers: section 4 identifies `RQM-mcp-client open`, `SX-egress-door open`, `ACF-consult-out`, and `ACF-why-export` as gaps, but section 7 lists only `B-claim-research-inherits-phase-deps`, `Bf9b9abac5b`, the docs-only `ddflow complete` pipeline, and a shell alias. The rule requires every discovered bug, misbehavior, or missing feature to be assessed and filed with a duplicate/not-corrected check; these gaps are only scheduled as future tasks or referenced as needs, so the phase-end assessment is incomplete.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md:113-133

chunk_findings.detail: [D-ddflow-self-assessment-r2] The self-assessment explicitly discovers a ddflow defect (“`ddflow complete` on a docs-only task still requires `implement`, `unit_tests` and `merge`”) and says the fix “is not on main yet,” so on the old ddflow this agent was still running on, the defect is neither corrected nor marked as already open. The decision requires discovered ddflow bugs to be filed without duplicates, but this bullet only says “Recorded honestly, not forced (see the task's gate record)” and gives no filed defect ID or existing-ticket cross-reference, unlike the two adjacent bullets that do (`already open, not re-filed` and `(filed)`). The defect therefore remains unfiled in violation of the assessment requirement.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md:132

chunk_findings.detail: The phase plan claims “The task graph was checked over the folded state: no cycles, every need exists” (line 120), but `ACF-e2e` (wave 3) depends only on “the four wave-2 build tasks.” `ACF-verify` is the wave-2 task that obtains operator access and resolves the otherwise UNKNOWN Accrete API/MCP/webhook/ingest-format questions. If `ACF-verify` remains operator-blocked, `ACF-e2e` still unlocks as soon as the four build tasks finish, leaving an “end-to-end Accrete integration” task with no documented external interface or access to test against, so its required dependency is missing and the graph claim is false.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md:117

chunk_findings.detail: The row “Data residency, which cloud, on-prem option, retention, training on customer data” is tagged `UNKNOWN`, whose definition earlier is `no evidence found`. The same row’s Source cell says “AWS and Azure named,” which is evidence about the cloud question. The mixed-evidence row is therefore mis-tagged under the document’s own VERIFIED/REPORTED/UNKNOWN scheme and should not use `UNKNOWN` for at least the cloud-provider portion.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/accrete.md:30
